narrative:
Your application was denied because the prediction estimated a 68% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. In practical terms, it judged that there was a roughly two-in-three chance you would struggle to repay, which is above the bank's acceptance threshold.

The decision was driven mainly by three things. The strongest was your credit record: it shows all past credits paid at the bank. Although that sounds favorable, it is very rare among approved applicants—only about 3% had that exact pattern—so it did not give the assessment the active, ongoing repayment signal it looks for, and it pushed toward bad risk. The next strongest was your checking account balance of 0–200 DM. That is less stable than the balances or account profiles of many approved applicants, so it also increased the perceived risk. The third was the purpose of the loan: a new car. Approved applicants more often requested loans for radio/TV or furniture, so this purpose made the application look slightly riskier.

Your requested amount, 1,264 DM, is well below the approved average, and a 15-month term is shorter than average, but these positives were not enough to offset the top concerns. To improve your chances, ask the bank which documents could clarify your credit history, consider adding a creditworthy co-applicant or guarantor, work on building a stronger checking or savings balance, and reapply after a period of consistent repayments. A smaller or more essential-purpose loan may also be viewed more favorably.
